title: The Peterman Pod × Ethan Evans — 同一份数字，两种叙事
title_en: The Peterman Pod × Ethan Evans — Same Numbers, Two Stories

questions.question: 一位工程师在会上总能把反对者辩倒，却渐渐被边缘化。按 Ethan Evans 对自己早年失败的复盘，最可能发生了什么？
options: 他的方案其实一直都是错的，组织最终用项目结果惩罚了他
经理嫉妒他的能力，在绩效评估里故意压低了他
对方不再跟他争，转去跟别人议论他，旁人没交情只点头
组织天然偏爱安静的人，任何有主张、敢争的人都会吃亏
questions.explanation: Evans 总结的机制是：推得太狠，反对者会停止跟你说话、转而跟别人说你；而你没在其他人那里建立关系，就没人回头替你说话。他并不认为该当好好先生，反而说经理常先升那个闹着要升的人。
questions.question_en: An engineer always wins arguments in meetings yet is gradually sidelined. Based on Ethan Evans's post-mortem of his own early failures, what most likely happened?
options_en: His proposals were actually always wrong, and the organization punished him through results
His manager envied his ability and deliberately marked him down in reviews
Opponents stopped arguing and talked about him to others, who just nodded along for lack of ties
Organizations naturally favor quiet people, so anyone who argues for a position loses out
questions.explanation_en: Evans's mechanism: push too hard and opponents stop talking to you and start talking about you; with no relationships built elsewhere, nobody comes back to speak up for you. He doesn't advise being a pushover, and even says managers often promote the one loudly pushing first.

questions.question: 你感觉上级正在给你攒 PIP 的材料。依这期节目里 Evans 的判断，哪种认识最贴近？
options: 公开表示要离职，经理为了留人通常会撤回 PIP
绩效没有客观读数，先讲故事者占上风；别指望 HR，处好或换经理
接受 PIP 并按计划改进，多数人都能借此翻身
拿出完整的工作数据和记录向 HR 申诉，客观数字最终会替你澄清
questions.explanation: Evans 说软件工程的绩效没有哪样是真正客观的，同一组数字能讲成两个故事，先手设定了叙事；跟记仇的上级斗等于拿刀去枪战，HR 不会来救你。他还说被 PIP 的人很少翻身。
questions.question_en: You sense your manager is building a PIP case against you. Which view best matches Evans's judgment in this episode?
options_en: Announce you're leaving, since managers usually withdraw a PIP to keep people
Performance has no objective reading and whoever tells the story first wins; don't count on HR — mend it or change managers
Accept the PIP and follow the plan, since most people turn things around that way
Take your full work data to HR, and the objective numbers will clear you in the end
questions.explanation_en: Evans says nothing about software performance is truly objective; the same numbers support two stories and moving first sets the narrative. Fighting a grudge-holding boss is bringing a knife to a gunfight, and HR won't rescue you. He also says few people survive a PIP.

questions.question: Evans 在 Appstore 那年对同事说「今年我会达成每一个目标，而它们毫无意义」。这句话揭示的结构是什么？
options: Amazon 的目标定得太低，说明中层管理者的能力普遍不足
他在刻意怠工，用完成指标来掩盖自己没有真正努力
只要中间目标全部达成，业务最终自然会走在正确方向上
评级激励让人争取稳拿的目标，真正重要却不会做的方向被绕开
questions.explanation: 他说为了评级和薪酬要肯定能拿下的目标，为了公司好却需要不知道怎么做的目标；真正的方向是在 Android 上和 Google 竞争，他拼命争取不被这条考核。考人和考事的数字都离本该代表的东西有一段距离。
questions.question_en: In his Appstore year Evans told a colleague, 'I'll hit every goal this year, and they're meaningless.' What structure does this reveal?
options_en: Amazon set its goals too low, showing that middle managers were broadly incompetent
He was deliberately slacking off, using met targets to hide that he wasn't really trying
As long as every intermediate goal is hit, the business will naturally end up heading the right way
Rating incentives push people toward safe goals and away from the vital ones nobody knows how to hit
questions.explanation_en: He says that for his rating and pay he wants goals he can nail, while the company needs goals no one knows how to achieve; the real aim, competing with Google on Android, was one he fought not to be measured on. Metrics for people and for projects both sit at a distance from what they're meant to represent.
